description: WHEN OTHER GO TO 9999-GOBACK: the default dispatch arm, and the one path through CBSTM03B that touches nothing at all (gate G48). THE ARM. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD (app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118) tests its arms in source order - 'TRNXFILE' (:119), 'XREFFILE' (:121), 'CUSTFILE' (:123), 'ACCTFILE' (:125) - and a name that matches none of the four falls to WHEN OTHER (:127), whose only statement is GO TO 9999-GOBACK (:128). Control leaves for :130-131 GOBACK without performing any of the four paragraphs, so the arm is reached by exclusion and is the only arm this case can be satisfied by. The DD name used here is 'NOSUCHDD', eight bytes like every other, and provably not one of the four. THE OMISSION THAT IS THE ASSERTION. Each of the four paragraphs ends by moving its own status into the caller's area at its nnn900-EXIT - TRNXFILE at :151-152, XREFFILE at :175-176, CUSTFILE at :200-201, ACCTFILE at :225-226 - and the GO TO jumps past all four. No MOVE <dd>FILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC runs, no READ INTO LK-M03B-FLDT runs, no file is opened or closed, and LK-M03B-RC and LK-M03B-FLDT therefore still hold exactly what the caller left in them. A translation that returned a '00' for an unknown DD, or an invented error status, or that cleared the record area, would all be new behaviour. WHY THE PRIOR VALUE MUST BE '10' AND NOT '00'. Asserting that a span is unchanged needs a prior value that cannot be mistaken for a fresh one, so the run first browses XREFFILE to end of file: OPEN INPUT XREF-FILE (:159-161) answers '00'; the first READ (:164-166) answers '00' and delivers the row; the second READ reaches AT END on a one-row dataset and answers '10' while leaving the receiving field untouched, because READ ... INTO moves nothing at end of file. Calls 4 and 5 then use the unrecognised name WITHOUT re-issuing the caller's MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC, and the answer is that same '10' and that same row. Had the prior status been a '00' - which is what an ACCTFILE CLOSE (:220-222) would have left - a stale '00' and a fresh '00' would be indistinguishable and the case would assert nothing. Call 5 repeats the point with 'O', an operation every arm supports, to show the arm is chosen by the DD name alone: a perfectly valid operation against an unknown DD is still nothing at all. THE CALLER'S SIDE. No caller in this repository drives this arm. CBSTM03A loads WS-M03B-DD with one of the four literals at all twelve of its call sites (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:347, :370, :394, :731, :766, :784, :802, :832, :857, :874, :890, :906), so the arm is dead from above and live only in the source - which is exactly why it is driven deliberately here rather than left unexercised. It matters because a stale status is not inert downstream: the four closes run back to back at :331, :333, :335 and :337, and 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE (:905-919) is the last of them, immediately before CLOSE STMT-FILE HTML-FILE (:339) and 9999-GOBACK (:341). Its test is IF WS-M03B-RC = '00' OR '04' (:911) - deliberately wider than the read-time EVALUATE WS-M03B-RC of 3000-ACCTFILE-GET (:403-410), which admits only '00' and WHEN OTHER - and anything else displays 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE' (:914) and abends through 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM (:916). A carried-over status would therefore fail a close that never failed. THE OPERATION SURFACE (gate G48). Across the twenty cases the four-file, six-operation contract is covered exhaustively as follows. OPEN on all four DD names: TRNXFILE in case01-case04, case16 and case20; XREFFILE in case07-case09, case18, case19 and case20; CUSTFILE in case10-case12 and case20; ACCTFILE in case13-case17 and case20. Sequential READ on the two ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL files: TRNXFILE in case02-case04, case16 and case20; XREFFILE in case07-case09, case18, case19 and case20. Keyed READ-K on the two ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM files: CUSTFILE in case10-case12 and case20; ACCTFILE in case13, case14, case16, case17 and case20. CLOSE on all four: TRNXFILE in case03, XREFFILE in case07 and case08, CUSTFILE in case10 and case20, ACCTFILE in case13. The operation a paragraph has no guard for, which reaches no IF and hands back the stale status: a plain READ on CUSTFILE in case12 and on ACCTFILE in case15. The two declared-and-dead codes: 'W' on ACCTFILE in case17, 'Z' on XREFFILE in case18. The four independent FILE STATUS areas: case20 (gate G47). And WHEN OTHER only here. The ACCTFILE close in particular - IF M03B-CLOSE (:220) reached only after IF M03B-OPEN (:208) and IF M03B-READ-K (:213) have both tested false, then CLOSE ACCT-FILE (:221), GO TO 4900-EXIT (:222), MOVE ACCTFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC (:226) and 4999-EXIT (:228-229, the program's final paragraph) - is pinned by case13, whose third call closes the file after a keyed read and answers '00' on the ACCTFILE-STATUS area alone (:95-97). Those three IF ... END-IF blocks carry no ELSE, so their declaration order is behaviour and the close guard is reachable only through the keyed-read guard (gate G30, rule R7). 'W' AND 'Z'. M03B-WRITE VALUE 'W' (:107) and M03B-REWRITE VALUE 'Z' (:108) are declared in the linkage area and tested by no IF in any of the four paragraphs; every SELECT is opened INPUT and no paragraph contains a WRITE or a REWRITE. They are SET nowhere in app/cbl either - CBSTM03A sets only OPEN, CLOSE, READ and READ-K (:348, :371, :395, :732, :744, :767, :785, :803, :833, :858, :875, :891, :907). They stay declared and unimplemented under practice B5, asserted as they actually behave - a silent no-op returning the file's stale status with the dataset unchanged - by case17 and case18, and neither code appears in this case. THE WIDTHS, re-derivable by hand. LK-M03B-AREA is 1040 = 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000 (:100-112), and all five images pin every one of those six spans by name at exactly those widths, trailing spaces included: LK-M03B-KEY is 25 spaces because none of these calls is keyed, and LK-M03B-KEY-LN PIC S9(4) carries the zoned image '000{' - four DISPLAY bytes rather than a two-byte halfword, the brace being the positive overpunch of a zero low-order digit. The XREFFILE record is 50 = 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 from app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, while app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt ships 36 bytes per row and omits the trailing FILLER PIC X(14); the case therefore declares the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation and the harness supplies that FILLER once, at seed time, before anything reads the row (gate G16). It is one of only two pads in the whole suite, the other being USRSEC 57 to 80. The seeded row is read back afterwards and pinned field by field across all four CVACT03Y spans with FILLER as 14 spaces - the read-only proof no area image could give, since all four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph writes (gate G21). Every byte is US-ASCII, the code page of the authoritative app/data/ASCII fixtures, and never a platform default. WHAT IS NOT HERE. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference and no CALL statement - it GOBACKs without touching one, and LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS and not a return code. expectedMessages is empty because CBSTM03B contains no DISPLAY statement at all; every diagnostic in the statement job, 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE' among them, is emitted by CBSTM03A, which is where the decision about what a status means lives. jobParameters is empty because it belongs to BATCH_JOB alone: the unit is a COMPONENT, a Spring @Component reached through its typed method and never through a JobLauncher or over HTTP (gates G12 and G51, requirement I3), whatever the mandated StatementGenerationJobB name suggests. No TRNXFILE, CUSTFILE or ACCTFILE input is seeded, because the WHEN OTHER arm opens nothing and a dataset no call can reach would be an input that asserts nothing. PROVENANCE. Every expected value above was derived statically - by structured reading of the line numbers cited, the CVACT03Y byte offsets and the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt - and was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the COBOL. That execution is empirically impossible here: cobc refuses CBSTM03B at :116 because PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LK-M03B-AREA is a subprogram entry rather than an executable main, its indexed file handler is reported disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists. AAP section 0.7.6 records the eight verified blockers and section 0.9.11 escalates the deviation as risk R-A: only the provenance of these values changes - 20 cases per program, field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module all stand. HOW THE CALL SCRIPT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HELD IN JAVA: the sequence of CALLs below used to live in a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant the case file did not describe the one thing it asserts - a subroutine whose entire contract is a DD name plus a one-character operation code IS its call sequence. Renumbering this file would have silently given it a different script, and a twenty-first case would have thrown from a default arm. unitStimulus.operationScript now carries it, one entry per CALL in issue order, each declaring LK-M03B-DD, the 88-level operation code from app/cbl/CBSTM03B.cbl:103-108, and where applicable LK-M03B-KEY and LK-M03B-KEY-LN. Two caller idioms are declared explicitly because the source distinguishes them: status '00' is the MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC every real call site issues, and its ABSENCE carries the previous call's status forward - the only way to observe a fall-through exit that assigns nothing new; primesRecordArea true is the MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT that app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L350, :L745 and :L834 issue, and its ABSENCE is the omission at :L857-860 that makes 'at end of file the record area is returned unchanged' an assertion with content. Every expected area image below was derived from this script by reading CBSTM03B's rules, never by running the Java.
